sentences.text: Gregory S. Paul estimated that this dinosaur measured 4.5 meters in length and weighed 200 kilograms.
The holotype ilium, which is the hip bone used to define the species, measures 37.5 centimeters long.
If the skull fragments belong to this animal, the head would have been approximately 60 centimeters long.
Matthew Carrano identified a unique trait where the suture between the pubic peduncle and pubic bone is convex at the front and concave at the rear.
One right ilium shows deformation likely caused by an injury, representing evidence of a pathology.
Another specimen possesses a pathological rib, indicating health issues in the population.
James Henry Madsen Jr. named the type species Marshosaurus bicentesimus in 1976.
The genus name Marshosaurus honors the paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh.
The specific name bicentesimus was chosen to honor the bicentennial of the United States of America.
The holotype specimen was found in the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation dating to approximately 155 to 152 million years ago.
The known fossil material represents at least three individuals of Marshosaurus.
A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild found no signs of stress fractures in five foot bones referred to Marshosaurus.
Roger Benson classified Marshosaurus as a megalosauroid in a 2010 phylogenetic analysis.
Marshosaurus is classified as a member of the family Piatnitzkysauridae.
Marshosaurus belongs to the class Reptilia.
Marshosaurus lived in the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of Utah and possibly Colorado.
The Morrison Formation, where Marshosaurus fossils are found, dates from the late Oxfordian to early Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic.
The environment of the Morrison Formation is interpreted as semiarid with distinct wet and dry seasons.
Marshosaurus lived between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages.
James Henry Madsen originally placed the phylogenetic position of Marshosaurus as uncertain within Theropoda.
